# Reference trace captured from the real Lua `game/online/match_driver.lua`,
# per v2/tools/lua_reference/README.md, driving a scripted sequence that
# forces a rollback: the star (a real `game/transport/fake_star.lua` pair
# from `game/online/match_driver_fixture.lua`'s `fixture.session("1v1")`)
# only pumps every 5 steps, so both peers predict the rows they have not
# received and correct them in one burst once the pump runs — the same
# `run_bursty` shape `spec/game/online_match_driver_spec.lua` uses to exercise
# rollback. Regenerate from a scratch copy of core/, sim/, data/, game/ with a
# headless conf.lua:
#
#   local match_driver = require("game.online.match_driver")
#   local fixture = require("game.online.match_driver_fixture")
#   local session = fixture.session("1v1")
#   -- build host/guest drivers via match_driver.new, advance() each step,
#   -- pump() the star every 5th step, print match_driver.diagnostics(driver)
#   -- and, every 10th step, match_driver.checkpoints(driver)'s newest hash.
#
# `rollback`/`correction` are `RollbackSessionDiagnostics.rollback_count`/
# `.correction_count` and only move at a pump step, confirming the burst
# shape actually predicted and then corrected. `hash <step> <peer> <tick>
# <digest>` lines are `match_snapshot.hash` at each 10-tick checkpoint; host
# and guest agree at every one (10, 20, ..., 90) — this is the real Lua
# proving out the exact claim the port needs to reproduce bit for bit.
#
# The Rust-side half of this comparison — building the same scenario through
# `gc_netcode::match_driver` and asserting its `diagnostics()`/`checkpoints()`
# match this trace tick for tick — is blocked: constructing a `MatchDriver`
# end to end needs `gc_netcode::coordinator` and `gc_netcode::protocol`
# (`NOT YET PORTED` placeholders as of this port, owned by concurrent
# agents). `tests/match_driver.rs`'s
# `match_driver_differential_matches_the_lua_reference` is `#[ignore]`d
# naming this exact blocker; re-enable it once those modules land, with this
# fixture already committed and ready to compare against.
#
# mode=1v1 host=host guest=guest_1
